A primitive's value is the JSON property itself (json.html#primitive: "the value of the primitive is represented as the property value"), so birthDate "2000-01-01" has one value and meets Patient.birthDate.value min 1; HL7 6.10.4 counts the value as absent.

HL7 6.10.4 accepts 'Element' everywhere.

The Composition conforms to Composition-uv-ips: section[14].entry[0] (LOINC 82810-3) is in no ValueSet of the pregnancyOutcome slice's required binding (pregnancies-summary-uv-ips enumerates its codes), so it matches pregnancyStatus alone. Under -tx n/a HL7 6.10.4 does not evaluate that binding, matches both slices, and so finds no entry for Bundle.entry:composition (plan A, IPS all-sections multi-match, withdrawn).

ElementDefinition.type.targetProfile: c references b, which references a, which does not conform, so c does not conform, whatever the entries' order. HL7 6.10.2 keeps c's answer computed assuming a conforms when a's referrer comes first.

bundle.html#references: when several entries match a reference "it is ambiguous which is correct", so the reference names no target whose type could be checked; it is reported as ambiguous (REFERENCE_MULTIPLE_MATCHES, as HL7 reports it). HL7 6.10.2 also checks the type of one of the entries it matches.

ElementDefinition.type.targetProfile: the target "must conform to at least one" of the profiles, and every Patient conforms to DomainResource, one of them. HL7 6.10.2 reports a Patient that does not conform to the other, a Patient profile.

HL7 6.10.2 keeps the answer computed under that assumption when the entries come in this order, and reports c's reference.

bundle.html#references: "If the reference is version specific (either relative or absolute), then remove the version from the URL before matching fullUrl, and then match the version based on Resource.meta.versionId": an absolute versioned reference resolves, and its target that does not conform is reported. HL7 6.10.2 removes the version only from relative references.

bundle.html#references: a relative reference resolves from the base of the RESTful fullUrl of the entry that holds the referring resource; from another base it names another resource, and from an entry with no RESTful fullUrl (urn:uuid, none) it "has no defined meaning". HL7 6.10.2's FHIRPath resolve() resolves from that base when it can, else finds an entry of the reference's type and id, in any base; its reference phase does not (tp_01, tp_04).
